# `cfmat.analytics`

<!-- generated by tools/gen_api_docs.py; do not edit -->

Market analytics: returns and performance metrics, technical indicators, candlestick and chart patterns, statistical tests and factor tools (M04, M06, M07).

```text
metrics      returns, Sharpe/Sortino/Calmar, drawdowns, PSR and deflated Sharpe
indicators   SMA/EMA/RSI/MACD/Bollinger/ATR, ADX, Supertrend, Donchian, Hurst ...
patterns     15 candlestick patterns, swing structure, double tops/bottoms, squeezes
stats        HAC t-statistics, Benjamini-Hochberg q-values, event studies
factors      cross-sectional factor tools: winsorise, z-score, neutralise, IC, quantiles
```

### `cfmat.analytics.factors`

Cross-sectional factor research on a (date, asset) panel (M07).

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `factor_summary` | `def factor_summary(ic: pd.Series, periods_per_year: int = 12) -> pd.Series` | Headline statistics of an IC series. |
| `information_coefficient` | `def information_coefficient(scores: pd.Series, fwd_returns: pd.Series) -> pd.Series` | Spearman rank correlation between scores and next-period returns, one value per date. |
| `neutralize` | `def neutralize(s: pd.Series, groups: pd.Series) -> pd.Series` | Subtract each (date, group) mean: the score no longer bets on groups (sectors). |
| `quantile_returns` | `def quantile_returns(scores: pd.Series, fwd_returns: pd.Series, q: int = 5) -> pd.DataFrame` | Mean next-period return of each score quantile (1 = lowest), one row per date. |
| `turnover` | `def turnover(scores: pd.Series, top: float = 0.2) -> pd.Series` | Fraction of the top-``top`` names on each date that were not in it the date before. |
| `winsorize` | `def winsorize(s: pd.Series, lower: float = 0.01, upper: float = 0.99) -> pd.Series` | Clip each date's cross-section at its ``lower`` and ``upper`` quantiles. |
| `zscore` | `def zscore(s: pd.Series, groups: pd.Series \| None = None) -> pd.Series` | Cross-sectional z-score per date, or per (date, group) when ``groups`` is given. |

### `cfmat.analytics.indicators`

Technical indicators, written out so learners can see every step.

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `adx` | `def adx(ohlc: pd.DataFrame, period: int = 14) -> pd.DataFrame` | Wilder's Average Directional Index with +DI and −DI. |
| `atr` | `def atr(ohlc: pd.DataFrame, period: int = 14) -> pd.Series` | Average True Range with Wilder smoothing. |
| `bollinger_bands` | `def bollinger_bands(close: pd.Series, window: int = 20, n_std: float = 2.0) -> pd.DataFrame` | Middle band (SMA) and bands ``n_std`` population standard deviations above and below. |
| `bollinger_bandwidth` | `def bollinger_bandwidth(close: pd.Series, window: int = 20, n_std: float = 2.0) -> pd.Series` | (upper − lower) / middle. Low values mark a volatility squeeze. |
| `donchian` | `def donchian(ohlc: pd.DataFrame, window: int = 20) -> pd.DataFrame` | Highest high and lowest low of the last ``window`` bars (including today). |
| `efficiency_ratio` | `def efficiency_ratio(close: pd.Series, window: int = 20) -> pd.Series` | Kaufman efficiency ratio: net move / total path length, in [0, 1]. Near 1 = clean trend, near 0 = choppy, range-bound. |
| `ema` | `def ema(series: pd.Series, span: int) -> pd.Series` | Exponential moving average with span ``span`` (no bias adjustment, like most charting tools). |
| `hurst_exponent` | `def hurst_exponent(series: pd.Series \| np.ndarray, max_lag: int = 50) -> float` | Hurst exponent of a (log) price series from the scaling of lagged differences. |
| `macd` | `def macd(close: pd.Series, fast: int = 12, slow: int = 26, signal: int = 9) -> pd.DataFrame` | MACD line (fast EMA − slow EMA), its signal line and the histogram. |
| `rate_of_change` | `def rate_of_change(close: pd.Series, window: int = 10) -> pd.Series` | Percentage change over ``window`` bars (×100). |
| `rolling_volatility` | `def rolling_volatility(close: pd.Series, window: int = 20, periods: int = 252) -> pd.Series` | Annualised volatility of log returns over a rolling window. |
| `rolling_zscore` | `def rolling_zscore(series: pd.Series, window: int) -> pd.Series` | How many rolling standard deviations the series is from its rolling mean. |
| `rsi` | `def rsi(close: pd.Series, period: int = 14) -> pd.Series` | Wilder's Relative Strength Index (0–100). |
| `sma` | `def sma(series: pd.Series, window: int) -> pd.Series` | Simple moving average over ``window`` bars. |
| `stochastic` | `def stochastic(ohlc: pd.DataFrame, k: int = 14, d: int = 3) -> pd.DataFrame` | Stochastic oscillator %K and %D (0–100). |
| `supertrend` | `def supertrend(ohlc: pd.DataFrame, period: int = 10, multiplier: float = 3.0) -> pd.DataFrame` | Supertrend: an ATR trailing line that flips sides when price closes through it. |
| `true_range` | `def true_range(ohlc: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | True range: the largest of high − low, \|high − previous close\| and \|low − previous close\|. |

### `cfmat.analytics.metrics`

Return and performance statistics.

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `annualized_volatility` | `def annualized_volatility(returns: pd.Series, periods: int = 252) -> float` | Sample standard deviation of returns scaled by √periods. |
| `cagr` | `def cagr(returns: pd.Series, periods: int = 252) -> float` | Compound annual growth rate. |
| `calmar_ratio` | `def calmar_ratio(returns: pd.Series, periods: int = 252) -> float` | CAGR divided by the absolute maximum drawdown (0 if there was no drawdown). |
| `deflated_sharpe_ratio` | `def deflated_sharpe_ratio(returns: pd.Series, n_trials: int, sr_variance: float) -> float` | PSR against the Sharpe you would expect from the best of ``n_trials`` random tries. |
| `drawdown_series` | `def drawdown_series(equity: pd.Series) -> pd.Series` | Fractional distance below the running peak (0 at new highs, negative otherwise). |
| `equity_curve` | `def equity_curve(returns: pd.Series, start_value: float = 1.0) -> pd.Series` | Growth of ``start_value`` when compounding ``returns``. |
| `expected_max_sharpe` | `def expected_max_sharpe(n_trials: int, sr_variance: float) -> float` | Expected maximum per-period Sharpe among ``n_trials`` skill-less strategies. |
| `hit_rate` | `def hit_rate(returns: pd.Series) -> float` | Share of non-zero periods that were profitable. |
| `log_returns` | `def log_returns(prices: pd.Series \| pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series \| pd.DataFrame` | Period-over-period log returns, dropping the first (empty) row. |
| `max_drawdown` | `def max_drawdown(equity: pd.Series) -> float` | Worst peak-to-trough loss as a negative fraction, e.g. -0.25 for 25%. |
| `performance_summary` | `def performance_summary(returns: pd.Series, rf: float = 0.0, periods: int = 252) -> pd.Series` | One-line tear sheet used throughout the course. |
| `probabilistic_sharpe_ratio` | `def probabilistic_sharpe_ratio(returns: pd.Series, sr_benchmark: float = 0.0) -> float` | Probability that the true (per-period) Sharpe exceeds ``sr_benchmark``. |
| `profit_factor` | `def profit_factor(returns: pd.Series) -> float` | Sum of gains divided by sum of losses (inf when there are no losses). |
| `sharpe_ratio` | `def sharpe_ratio(returns: pd.Series, rf: float = 0.0, periods: int = 252) -> float` | Annualised Sharpe ratio. ``rf`` is an annual risk-free rate. |
| `simple_returns` | `def simple_returns(prices: pd.Series \| pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series \| pd.DataFrame` | Period-over-period simple returns, dropping the first (empty) row. |
| `sortino_ratio` | `def sortino_ratio(returns: pd.Series, rf: float = 0.0, periods: int = 252) -> float` | Like Sharpe, but only downside deviation counts as risk. |

### `cfmat.analytics.patterns`

Candlestick and chart-structure patterns (M06, M12).

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `bearish_engulfing` | `def bearish_engulfing(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Yesterday bullish, today bearish with a body covering yesterday's body, after a rise. |
| `bearish_marubozu` | `def bearish_marubozu(bars: pd.DataFrame, min_body: float = 0.9) -> pd.Series` | Down candle whose body fills at least ``min_body`` of the day's range. |
| `bullish_engulfing` | `def bullish_engulfing(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Yesterday bearish, today bullish with a body covering yesterday's body. |
| `bullish_marubozu` | `def bullish_marubozu(bars: pd.DataFrame, min_body: float = 0.9) -> pd.Series` | Up candle whose body fills at least ``min_body`` of the day's range. |
| `consolidation` | `def consolidation(bars: pd.DataFrame, window: int = 20, max_width: float = 0.06) -> pd.Series` | Range-bound box: the last ``window`` bars fit inside ``max_width`` of price. |
| `dark_cloud_cover` | `def dark_cloud_cover(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Bullish day, then a bearish day opening above its high and closing below its midpoint. |
| `doji` | `def doji(bars: pd.DataFrame, max_body: float = 0.1) -> pd.Series` | Open ≈ close: body at most ``max_body`` of the day's range (indecision). |
| `double_bottom` | `def double_bottom(bars: pd.DataFrame, k: int = 3, tolerance: float = 0.02, lookback: int = 60) -> pd.Series` | Two confirmed swing lows within ``tolerance`` of each other inside ``lookback`` bars, completed when the close breaks above the highest high between them (the neckline). |
| `double_top` | `def double_top(bars: pd.DataFrame, k: int = 3, tolerance: float = 0.02, lookback: int = 60) -> pd.Series` | Two swing highs within ``tolerance`` of each other, completed when price closes below the trough between them. |
| `evening_star` | `def evening_star(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Strong up candle, a small-bodied candle, then a down candle closing below the first one's midpoint. |
| `hammer` | `def hammer(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Small body near the high, long lower shadow (≥ 2× body), after a decline. |
| `higher_highs_lows` | `def higher_highs_lows(bars: pd.DataFrame, k: int = 3) -> pd.Series` | Uptrend structure: the last confirmed swing high and swing low are both above the ones before them. |
| `inside_bar` | `def inside_bar(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Today's range lies inside yesterday's range. |
| `lower_highs_lows` | `def lower_highs_lows(bars: pd.DataFrame, k: int = 3) -> pd.Series` | True while the latest confirmed swing high and swing low are both lower than the previous ones. |
| `morning_star` | `def morning_star(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Long bearish candle, small-bodied candle, then a bullish candle closing above the first candle's midpoint. |
| `outside_bar` | `def outside_bar(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Today's range engulfs yesterday's range. |
| `piercing_line` | `def piercing_line(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Bearish day, then a bullish day opening below its low and closing above its midpoint. |
| `scan` | `def scan(bars: pd.DataFrame, names: list[str] \| None = None) -> pd.DataFrame` | Evaluate many patterns at once (one boolean column each). |
| `shooting_star` | `def shooting_star(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Small body near the low, long upper shadow (≥ 2× body), after a rise. |
| `squeeze` | `def squeeze(bars: pd.DataFrame, window: int = 20, lookback: int = 120, tolerance: float = 1.05) -> pd.Series` | Bollinger bandwidth within ``tolerance`` of its ``lookback``-bar low: volatility is compressed and a breakout (either way) often follows. |
| `swing_highs` | `def swing_highs(bars: pd.DataFrame, k: int = 3) -> pd.Series` | Price of each swing high (a high above the k highs on both sides), placed on the bar where it is *confirmed* (k bars later). NaN elsewhere. |
| `swing_lows` | `def swing_lows(bars: pd.DataFrame, k: int = 3) -> pd.Series` | Swing-low prices, flagged ``k`` bars after the low (when it is first known). |
| `three_black_crows` | `def three_black_crows(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Three falling down candles, each opening inside the previous body. |
| `three_white_soldiers` | `def three_white_soldiers(bars: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series` | Three rising bullish candles, each opening inside the previous body. |

### `cfmat.analytics.stats`

Statistical tests that research code needs again and again (M04, M06, M07, M23).

| Name | Signature | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `benjamini_hochberg` | `def benjamini_hochberg(pvalues: pd.Series) -> pd.Series` | False-discovery-rate adjusted p-values (q-values). |
| `event_study` | `def event_study(close: pd.Series, events: pd.Series, horizons: tuple[int, ...] = (1, 5, 10, 20), n_perm: int = 1000, seed: int = 0) -> pd.DataFrame` | Forward returns after event days compared with the other days. |
| `hac_tstat` | `def hac_tstat(x: pd.Series \| np.ndarray, lags: int \| None = None) -> float` | t-statistic of ``mean(x)`` with Newey-West standard errors (Bartlett kernel). |
